              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
              text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
              text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                (Mosaic buys Harbor's assets)
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
              text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
              text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
                for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
                must confirm.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec

            questions:
            - question_id: Q-SAR
              text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
              consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item;
                they can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close
                and could affect the deal itself.
              state: answered
              answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
                in diligence.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-070aec
            - question_id: Q-KYC
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations?
              consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
                gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
                obligations for these users.
              state: answered
              answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
                reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-620c62
            - question_id: Q-MTL
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers?
              consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
                on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
                question.
              state: answered
              answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
                for the four new markets.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-771ee1

              consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
                disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
              revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
              file_revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

              passages: &id034
              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

          title: facts.md

          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

    available_excerpt: "# Research this issue for the dossier: Purchase-agreement
      authority and risk\n\n## Question\n\nResearch this issue for the dossier: Purchase-agreement
      authority and risk allocation. Pre-close data transfers, testing, customer communications,
      or operating changes could conflict with transaction covenants, consent limits,
      closing conditions, or liability allocations.\nLawyer's accepted priorities

            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
              text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts

              text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase

              text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on

                text: '# Issues and workstreams


                  - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                  under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                  transfer/survive the acquisition

                  - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                  missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                  Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                  - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                  Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                  - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                  when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                  - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                  money transmission or consumer protection implications

                  - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                  -->

                  - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-8f6233be11b7205ffc25.md
              revision: 23fcb27105945705c2b19c1547c310303a49b7d909b07a52e0fe3323e0ae2e9a

              - start: 0
                end: 2312
                text: '## Preparation note


                  **Result:** Legal and compliance review is required before the Nov
                  15 close. The migration is not only a technical data transfer.


                  **Lawyer reframe:** Determine which pre-close and day-one actions
                  could change the deal risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken
                  anti-money-laundering controls, or harm customers. Then separate
                  safe preparation from actions that require legal clearance.


                  The current plan relies on unconfirmed assumptions. Harbor’s licenses
                  might not transfer in an asset purchase. Mosaic might not be able
                  to rely on Harbor’s identity checks. About 40 alerts and several
                  suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed. Harbor’s monitoring
                  service will end at close, but the replacement has not been shown
                  to work.


                  The safer route is a staged launch. Mosaic can complete reversible
                  technical work before close. It should delay affected accounts,
                  new markets, or full product access if a legal or compliance gate
                  remains open.


                  ### Material issues


                  - Unresolved alerts and suspicious activity history.

                  - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase.

                  - Reliance on identity checks that lack underlying records.

                  - Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.

                  - Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.

                  - Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.


                  ### Three business priorities


                  1. **Protect the acquisition decision.** Review unresolved compliance
                  matters before Mosaic accepts risk that is difficult to reverse.

                  2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify that Mosaic can serve
                  each account and market after an asset purchase.

                  3. **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit
                  a staged launch if any required control is not ready.


                  ### First three issues to research


                  1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The findings
                  could change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or account
                  eligibility.

                  2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could take time and
                  could prevent launch in the four new markets.

                  3. **Identity-verification reliance.** Missing source records affect
                  240,000 consumers and 12,000 business accounts and could require
                  re-verification or access limits.




                  > A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used
                  the material available.

                  '
              source_version: 23fcb27105945705c2b19c1547c310303a49b7d909b07a52e0fe3323e0ae2e9a

              revision: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73
              file_revision: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73

              availability: selected_passage

              passages: &id039
              - start: 0
                end: 5937
                text: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov 15)


                  **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
                  migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest
                  turn ("Generate the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds
                  comparisons are supporting work; they do not change that question.
                  The record contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered
                  issues are `open`, and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is
                  structured — was left open with no answer.


                  **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data
                  migration." The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated
                  event: on day 1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its
                  own licensed product set with no re-verification, repoints monitoring,
                  and launches a cash offer — under an asset-purchase structure in
                  which nothing about Harbor''s licenses or compliance record transfers
                  by default. The operative question is therefore not "can we inherit
                  Harbor''s status," but **"what must Mosaic obtain, file, decide
                  or preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts of the
                  stated deal upside are not actually available at close."**


                  **Three premises the record lets us test**


                  1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment
                  CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to
                  252k accounts.

                  2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on
                  the arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state
                  union yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are
                  never named; and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests
                  on an assumption the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]),
                  against the saved position that transferability should not be relied
                  on without a state rule, approval or written regulator position.

                  3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved.
                  Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown,
                  and the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in
                  2024; only pass/fail survives).


                  **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9
                  weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and
                  preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and
                  schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate
                  the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
                  new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
                  only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient
                  accounts with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full one.


                  **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing
                  (44-state footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users;
                  SAR and alert handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring
                  vendor transition at close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing
                  and material: **migration data handling and customer notice** (the
                  piece the request actually calls "just a data migration," never
                  analyzed); **pre-close papering** (closing conditions, interim operation,
                  allocation of the alert/SAR and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms
                  appear anywhere); and **post-close access to Harbor''s alert/case
                  history** (the records live in the SaaS system whose contract ends
                  at close).


                  **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business
                  question, time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


                  1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else
                  is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the deal itself;
                  it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a filing is
                  late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed to answer
                  it may become inaccessible at close.

                  2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify,
                  or restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification"
                  is available at all for the largest population; the underlying documents
                  cannot be recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a
                  multi-week program that has to be decided before close, not after.

                  3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull
                  them from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being
                  sold on, state timelines are the longest external dependency and
                  cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority is a
                  violation later paperwork cannot undo.


                  **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
                  KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the
                  licensing position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
                  — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go
                  decision, licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow
                  the backlog read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market
                  access.


                  **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
                  and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path,
                  and some prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions
                  are not findings about this acquisition. The licensing research
                  has **no citable support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read;
                  one output headed "No external authority retrieved"), and repeated
                  "research queued/running" messages are status, not results. Assumption
                  [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still calls the structure unconfirmed
                  although the asset purchase is recorded and was reconfirmed twice
                  by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field (2026-09-11) sits
                  oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat it as unverified.
                  Urgent below marks the five items where the close date itself fixes
                  the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards; it is not
                  the same as the top-three ranking.


                  *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
                  facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing
                  packet was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated
                  as fallible synthesis.*

                  '
              source_version: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73

              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

          title: DOR-20260912-049f9c.md
          support_state: supplied
          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '## Preparation note


            **Result:** Legal and compliance review is required before the Nov 15
            close. The migration is not only a technical data transfer.


            **Lawyer reframe:** Determine which pre-close and day-one actions could
            change the deal risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken anti-money-laundering
            controls, or harm customers. Then separate safe preparation from actions
            that require legal clearance.


            The current plan relies on unconfirmed assumptions. Harbor’s licenses
            might not transfer in an asset purchase. Mosaic might not be able to rely
            on Harbor’s identity checks. About 40 alerts and several suspicious activity
            reports remain unreviewed. Harbor’s monitoring service will end at close,
            but the replacement has not been shown to work.


            The safer route is a staged launch. Mosaic can complete reversible technical
            work before close. It should delay affected accounts, new markets, or
            full product access if a legal or compliance gate remains open.


            ### Material issues


            - Unresolved alerts and suspicious activity history.

            - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase.

            - Reliance on identity checks that lack underlying records.

            - Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.

            - Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.

            - Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.


            ### Three business priorities


            1. **Protect the acquisition decision.** Review unresolved compliance
            matters before Mosaic accepts risk that is difficult to reverse.

            2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify that Mosaic can serve each
            account and market after an asset purchase.

            3. **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged
            launch if any required control is not ready.


            ### First three issues to research


            1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The findings could
            change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or account eligibility.

            2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could take time and could
            prevent launch in the four new markets.

            3. **Identity-verification reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000
            consumers and 12,000 business accounts and could require re-verification
            or access limits.




            > A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material
            available.

            '

          available_excerpt: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov 15)


            **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
            migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest turn ("Generate
            the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds comparisons are supporting
            work; they do not change that question. The record contains **no recorded
            decisions** at all, all five registered issues are `open`, and one intake
            question — how the $50 bonus is structured — was left open with no answer.


            **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data migration."
            The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated event: on day 1 Mosaic
            Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its own licensed product set with
            no re-verification, repoints monitoring, and launches a cash offer — under
            an asset-purchase structure in which nothing about Harbor''s licenses
            or compliance record transfers by default. The operative question is therefore
            not "can we inherit Harbor''s status," but **"what must Mosaic obtain,
            file, decide or preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts
            of the stated deal upside are not actually available at close."**


            **Three premises the record lets us test**


            1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment CIP,
            licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to 252k accounts.

            2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on the
            arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state union
            yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are never named;
            and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests on an assumption
            the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]), against the
            saved position that transferability should not be relied on without a
            state rule, approval or written regulator position.

            3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved. Whether
            Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and the pre-2023
            records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024; only pass/fail
            survives).


            **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9 weeks
            as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and preserve the
            alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and schedule remediation;
            prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate the monitoring cutover
            with a parallel run; paper notice/consent, new customer terms and closing
            conditions. If a gate fails, migrate only in the overlapping states on
            day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts with limits — a scoped migration
            rather than the full one.


            **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state
            footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert
            handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition at
            close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
            data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually calls
            "just a data migration," never analyzed); **pre-close papering** (closing
            conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR and KYC-record
            risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close access to
            Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS system whose
            contract ends at close).


            **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business question,
            time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


            1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else is scheduled.**
            It is the only item that can change the deal itself; it is entirely unread,
            so no one can yet say whether a filing is late or an account must be excluded;
            and the records needed to answer it may become inaccessible at close.

            2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify, or
            restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification" is available
            at all for the largest population; the underlying documents cannot be
            recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week program
            that has to be decided before close, not after.

            3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull them
            from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being sold on, state
            timelines are the longest external dependency and cannot be compressed,
            and serving a state without authority is a violation later paperwork cannot
            undo.


            **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
            KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
            position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
            — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
            licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog read,
            because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.


            **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
            and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and some
            prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions are not
            findings about this acquisition. The licensing research has **no citable
            support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output headed "No
            external authority retrieved"), and repeated "research queued/running"
            messages are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b]
            still calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase is recorded
            and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field
            (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat it
            as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where the close date
            itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards; it
            is not the same as the top-three ranking.


            *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
            facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing packet
            was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated as fallible synthesis.*

            '

          title: facts.md

          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

              passages: &id041
              - start: 0
                end: 1441
                text: '# Issues and workstreams


                  - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                  under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                  transfer/survive the acquisition

                  - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                  missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                  Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                  - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                  Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                  - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                  when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                  - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                  money transmission or consumer protection implications

                  - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                  -->

                  - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
                  <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

                  - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->

                  - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
                  -->

                  - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
                  -->

                  - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
                  -->

                  - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->

                  '
              source_version: 916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac

              passages: &id042
              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

            - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
            underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
            CIP/AML obligations

            - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
            ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

            - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
            the SaaS contract terminates at close

            - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money
            transmission or consumer protection implications

            - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
            -->

            - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
            <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

            - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf

            - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2

          title: facts.md
          support_state: supplied
          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

            questions:
            - question_id: Q-SAR
              text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
              consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item;
                they can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close
                and could affect the deal itself.
              state: answered
              answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
                in diligence.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-070aec
            - question_id: Q-KYC
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations?
              consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
                gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
                obligations for these users.
              state: answered
              answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
                reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-620c62
            - question_id: Q-MTL
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers?
              consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
                on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
                question.
              state: answered
              answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
                for the four new markets.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-771ee1
            - question_id: Q-BONUS
              text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
              consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
                disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.

              passages: &id043
              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                text: '# Issues and workstreams


                  - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                  under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                  transfer/survive the acquisition

                  - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                  missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                  Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                  - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                  Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                  - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                  when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                  - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                  money transmission or consumer protection implications

                  - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                  -->

                  - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
                  <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

                  - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->

                  - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
                  -->

                  - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
                  -->

                  - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
                  -->

                  - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->

                  '

                text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01
                  License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business
                  of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out
                  as providing money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder
                  this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA
                  person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed under
                  \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred by a
                  written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is
                  exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money
                  transmission outside the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license
                  issued under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection
                  5.02 Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent
                  licensing between [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner]
                  is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing
                  provisions of this [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other
                  states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes;
                  \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing
                  cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that
                  such protocols are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order
                  to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized
                  and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts with NMLS
                  or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
                  to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
                  licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees;
                  and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees
                  or other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
                  is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of
                  licensing in accordance with this [Act], including but not limited
                  to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control,
                  surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"

                text: "19 \n \n(C) \nEmployment history; \n(D) \nMedia history, including
                  an electronic search of national and \nlocal publications, wire
                  services, and business applications; and \n(E) \nFinancial services-related
                  regulatory history, including but \nnot limited to, money transmission,
                  securities, banking, insurance, and mortgage-\nrelated industries.
                  \nSection 5.05 Issuance of License. \n(a) \nWhen an application
                  for an original license under this [Act] appears to \ninclude all
                  the items and addresses all of the matters that are required, the
                  application is complete \nand the [Commissioner] shall promptly
                  notify the applicant in a record of the date on which the \napplication
                  is determined to be complete, and:13 \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
                  shall approve or deny the application within \n120 days after the
                  completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or
                  denied within 120 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe
                  application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe license takes effect as
                  of the first business day after \nexpiration of the 120-day period.
                  \n(C) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the \napplication
                  period. \n(b) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application
                  is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that the
                  application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems,
                  including the Criminal Background Check response from the FBI, and
                  address all of the \nmatters that are required, and is not an assessment
                  of the substance of the application or of the \nsufficiency of the
                  information provided. \n(c) \nWhen an application is filed and considered
                  complete under this [Section \n5.05], the [Commissioner] shall investigate
                  the applicant's financial condition and responsibility, \nfinancial
                  and business experience, character, and general fitness. The [Commissioner]
                  may \nconduct an on-site investigation of the applicant, the reasonable
                  cost of which the applicant must \npay. The [Commissioner] shall
                  issue a license to an applicant under this [Section 5.05] if the
                  \n[Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions have
                  been fulfilled: \n \n13 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
                  the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and
                  when states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this
                  [Act] is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an application
                  is determined to be complete.\n"
