                text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal
                  report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change
                  in information submitted by the licensee in its original license
                  \napplication which has not been reported to the [Commissioner].
                  \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an extension
                  of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
                  and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided
                  that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06].
                  \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does
                  not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements
                  that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
                  the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's license
                  in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act] or
                  other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation. \n(b)
                  \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate
                  that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee
                  must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02,
                  and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control
                  and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control.
                  \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
                  to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval
                  of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual
                  is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
                  to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual
                  becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b)
                  \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
                  control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee:
                  \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed
                  by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee
                  of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the
                  [Commissioner] may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of
                  persons acting in concert, to submit some or all information required
                  by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without
                  using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)]
                  shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new
                  key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements
                  of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"

                text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                  under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and
                  address all of the matters that are required, the application shall
                  \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify
                  the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
                  was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
                  shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the
                  completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or
                  denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application
                  is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting
                  in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe
                  [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod.
                  \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application
                  is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that the
                  application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems
                  and address all of the matters that are required, and is not an
                  assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
                  of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed
                  and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner]
                  shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial
                  \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the
                  person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire
                  control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control
                  \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that
                  all of the following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe
                  requirements of subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable;
                  and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial
                  and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
                  of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking
                  to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
                  general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be
                  in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate
                  that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit the person,
                  or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee.
                  \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to
                  a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate
                  and streamline the process of communicating when applications are
                  \nreceived and when states consider them to have been complete.
                  The intent of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin
                  on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"

                text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and
                  encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
                  state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
                  state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards;
                  or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
                  is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
                  to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement
                  through the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner]
                  shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication
                  to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny
                  the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice
                  of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
                  An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under
                  this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after
                  receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant to state
                  administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section
                  6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA
                  person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a
                  \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares
                  or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a
                  licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee by
                  devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
                  as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator,
                  or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent
                  jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt
                  under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner]
                  determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public
                  interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities of a licensee
                  or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization
                  of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person
                  in control of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in
                  [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the
                  \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days after
                  the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
                  procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived
                  from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should
                  be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
                  Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS
                  record.\n"

                  acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be
                  acquired will not implement any material \nchanges to its business
                  plan as a result of the acquisition of control, and if the person
                  \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement
                  any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition

                  in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A),
                  (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the
                  [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within
                  30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be
                  complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an
                  application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson
                  may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as
                  to whether the person \nwould be considered a person in control
                  of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If
                  the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
                  in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
                  is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)]
                  of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes

                  avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
                  \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                  to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
                  with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for
                  the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

          title: issues.md
          support_state: supplied
          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: '# Issues and workstreams


            - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
            the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
            the acquisition

            - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
            underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
            CIP/AML obligations

            - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
            ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

            - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
            the SaaS contract terminates at close

            - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money
            transmission or consumer protection implications

            - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
            -->

            - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
            <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

            - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf
            -->

            - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
            -->

            - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
            -->

            - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
            -->

            - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481
            -->

            '

          source_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545

          unit_id: p000014
          locator: Page 14, characters 0–1963
          available_excerpt: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection
            5.01 License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business
            of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing
            money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b)
            \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized
            delegate of a person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope
            of authority conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2)
            \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage
            in money transmission outside the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license
            issued under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection
            5.02 Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing
            between [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized
            and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
            [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted
            this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate
            in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination among
            state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent with this
            \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner]
            is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
            with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
            to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
            licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and
            \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or other
            \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
            and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance
            with this [Act], including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
            for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history
            background\n"

          unit_id: p000019
          locator: Page 19, characters 0–2376
          available_excerpt: "19 \n \n(C) \nEmployment history; \n(D) \nMedia history,
            including an electronic search of national and \nlocal publications, wire
            services, and business applications; and \n(E) \nFinancial services-related
            regulatory history, including but \nnot limited to, money transmission,
            securities, banking, insurance, and mortgage-\nrelated industries. \nSection
            5.05 Issuance of License. \n(a) \nWhen an application for an original
            license under this [Act] appears to \ninclude all the items and addresses
            all of the matters that are required, the application is complete \nand
            the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of
            the date on which the \napplication is determined to be complete, and:13
            \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within
            \n120 days after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is
            not approved or denied within 120 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A)
            \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe license takes effect as
            of the first business day after \nexpiration of the 120-day period. \n(C)
            \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the \napplication period.
            \n(b) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete
            and \nis accepted for processing means only that the application, on its
            face, appears to include all of the \nitems, including the Criminal Background
            Check response from the FBI, and address all of the \nmatters that are
            required, and is not an assessment of the substance of the application
            or of the \nsufficiency of the information provided. \n(c) \nWhen an application
            is filed and considered complete under this [Section \n5.05], the [Commissioner]
            shall investigate the applicant's financial condition and responsibility,
            \nfinancial and business experience, character, and general fitness. The
            [Commissioner] may \nconduct an on-site investigation of the applicant,
            the reasonable cost of which the applicant must \npay. The [Commissioner]
            shall issue a license to an applicant under this [Section 5.05] if the
            \n[Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions have been
            fulfilled: \n \n13 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the
            process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
            consider them to have been complete. The intent of this [Act] is for the
            application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined
            to be complete.\n"

          unit_id: p000021
          locator: Page 21, characters 0–2389
          available_excerpt: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
            The renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material
            change in information submitted by the licensee in its original license
            \napplication which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c)
            \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal
            \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize
            NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality is
            consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
            \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or
            satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money
            transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's
            license in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act]
            or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation. \n(b)
            \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that
            it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all
            times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of
            this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual
            \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of
            persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee
            shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring
            control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee
            and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that
            individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness.
            \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
            control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1)
            \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner];
            and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the request for approval.
            \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit a licensee or the
            person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert, to submit some or all
            information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)]
            without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)]
            shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key
            individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section
            5.04] for a licensee.\n"

          unit_id: p000022
          locator: Page 22, characters 0–2612
          available_excerpt: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of
            control under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and
            address all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe
            considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant
            in a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined to be
            complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the
            application within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif
            the application is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion
            date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or
            group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring
            control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application
            \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application
            is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that the application,
            on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address all of
            the matters that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance
            of \nthe application or of the sufficiency of the information provided.
            \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and considered complete under [Section
            \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition
            and responsibility, financial \nand business experience, character, and
            general fitness of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert,
            seeking to acquire control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition
            of control \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds
            that all of the following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe
            requirements of subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable;
            and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial and
            business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness of the
            person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to acquire control;
            and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness of the
            key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
            after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of
            the public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert,
            to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise
            subject to a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate
            and streamline the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived
            and when states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this
            Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an application
            is determined to be complete.\n"

          unit_id: p000023
          locator: Page 23, characters 0–2523
          available_excerpt: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized
            and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
            state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
            state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2)
            \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized
            and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)]
            and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through the multistate licensing
            process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice
            of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty (30)
            days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall
            set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial
            of the \napplication. An applicant whose application is denied by the
            [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty
            (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant
            to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section
            6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person
            that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
            meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
            of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
            that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person
            that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian,
            guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt
            of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that
            is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner]
            determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest;
            \n(6) \nA public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control
            of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in
            control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the
            licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3),
            (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
            within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
            Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision may
            be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
            should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
            Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

          source_hash: 4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680
          source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 24,
            characters 0–2799'
          unit_id: p000024
          locator: Page 24, characters 0–2799
          available_excerpt: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1)
            \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
            that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
            \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
            application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB
            accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided
            that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended or
            \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended while
            the person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B)
            \nif the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas received
            at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its most recent \nexamination
            by an MSB accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee
            to be acquired is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01,
            10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is
            completed, and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
            is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
            and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed;
            \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement any material \nchanges
            to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control, and if
            the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also will
            not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result
            of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice
            of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section
            6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed
            by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within
            30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete,
            the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for
            approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing
            a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould
            be considered a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a
            proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person
            would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person
            and transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
            and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes
            a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails
            itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess:
            \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept the
            \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state with sufficient
            staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section
            6.01(m)]; or\n"

          inputs:
            business_question:
              question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
              text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
                review before the Nov 15 close?
              revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
            facts:
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
              text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
              text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
              text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by
                Harbor.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
              text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
              text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
              text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed
                at Mosaic's engine on day 1.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
              text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
              text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
              source_ids:
              - REQ-20260909-283892
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
              text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
              text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC'd.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
              text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
              text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay's engine on day 1.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
              text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-9835ba
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
              text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                (Mosaic buys Harbor's assets)
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
              text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
              text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
                for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
                must confirm.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
              text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and
                SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor's licenses for the four new markets.
              source_ids:
              - MSG-20260909-2e549e
              origin: null
              verification_status: null
            assumptions:

            questions:
            - question_id: Q-SAR
              text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
              consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item;
                they can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close
                and could affect the deal itself.
              state: answered
              answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
                in diligence.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-070aec
            - question_id: Q-KYC
              text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations?
              consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
                gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
                obligations for these users.
              state: answered
              answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
                reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-620c62
            - question_id: Q-MTL
              text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers?
              consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
                on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
                question.
              state: answered
              answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
                for the four new markets.
              answer_kind: reported_fact
              linked_fact_ids:
              - FACT-20260909-771ee1
            - question_id: Q-BONUS
              text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
              consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
                disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
              state: left_open

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-df5dd9f25cf0547e2d1e.md

              passages: &id052
              - start: 0
                end: 3962
                text: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '
              source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

              - start: 0

                text: '# Issues and workstreams


                  - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                  under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                  transfer/survive the acquisition

                  - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                  missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                  Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                  - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                  Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                  - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                  when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                  - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                  money transmission or consumer protection implications

                  - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                  -->

                  '

                text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                  or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                  certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant that
                  is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the
                  certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order
                  the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find
                  necessary to enable the independent or certified public accountant
                  or \nindependent public accountant to remove the qualification.
                  \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee
                  shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45 days \nof
                  the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
                  and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report
                  required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
                  is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b)
                  \nThe authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum, each
                  authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer
                  employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier;
                  \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business
                  conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name;
                  \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart
                  date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting
                  as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court
                  orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information
                  the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized
                  delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary:
                  This language is designed to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform
                  Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States
                  are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting
                  requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize
                  reporting of significant events.\n"

                text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                  within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know
                  of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing
                  of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States
                  Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified
                  from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe
                  filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
                  the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding
                  for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making of a general
                  assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement
                  of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a state or
                  country in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed.
                  \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within
                  three business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the
                  occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or]
                  conviction of the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in
                  control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction
                  of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy
                  Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file
                  all reports required by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping,
                  and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set forth in the
                  Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining to
                  money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
                  report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
                  \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
                  7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the
                  following records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act]
                  for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding
                  money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted
                  at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income,
                  and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
                  records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

                  specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside this state
                  \nif they are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days'
                  notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained
                  by the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open
                  to inspection by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)].
                  \n \nARTICLE VIII \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship
                  Between Licensee and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section
                  8.01], \"remit\" means to make direct payments of money to \na licensee
                  or its representative authorized to receive money or to deposit
                  money in a bank in an \naccount specified by the licensee. \n(b)
                  \nBefore a licensee is authorized to conduct business through an
                  authorized \ndelegate or allows a person to act as the licensee's
                  authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update
                  as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably designed
                  to ensure that the licensee's authorized delegates comply with \napplicable
                  state and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract that
                  complies with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct a reasonable
                  risk-based background investigation sufficient \nfor the licensee
                  to determine whether the authorized delegate has complied and will
                  likely \ncomply with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn
                  authorized delegate must operate in full compliance with this [Act].
                  \n(d) \nThe written contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must
                  be signed by the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and, at
                  a minimum, must:\n"

                text: "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a

                  \nCopies of any non-confidential final orders of the [Department]
                  \nrelating to any violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing
                  this [Act]; and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or
                  penalty under this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe
                  [Commissioner] may conduct an examination or investigation of a
                  \nlicensee or authorized delegate or otherwise take independent
                  action authorized by this [Act] or by \na rule adopted or order
                  issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary or appropriate to
                  administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing this
                  [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy Act
                  and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct
                  an examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner]
                  may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction
                  with an examination \nconducted by representatives of other state
                  agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal government;
                  \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another state agency
                  or an agency \nof another state or of the federal government, or
                  a report prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which on
                  being accepted is considered for all purposes as an official report
                  \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under oath
                  a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
                  and require the person to produce records regarding any \nmatter
                  related to the condition and business of the licensee or authorized
                  delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate shall provide,
                  and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and complete access to,
                  all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably require to \nconduct
                  a complete examination. The records must be provided at the location
                  and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner], provided, the
                  [Commissioner] may utilize multistate record \nproduction standards
                  and examination procedures when such standards will reasonably achieve
                  \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless otherwise
                  directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee shall pay all \ncosts
                  reasonably incurred in connection with an examination of the licensee
                  or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner] is encouraged
                  to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination requests in
                  \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee to obtain records
                  located outside of the U.S., including but not limited \nto evidence

                  as provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"

          available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


            - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
            out).

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
            and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

            - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

            - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
            Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
            pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
            Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

            - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
            launching close+1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

            - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
            Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

            - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
            already KYC''d.

            - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
            results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
            onboarded before 2023.

            - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
            terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
            Relay''s engine on day 1.

            - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
            last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

            - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
            buys Harbor''s assets)

            - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
            institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
            required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

            - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
            last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
            Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
            own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

            - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
            is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
            and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
            AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
            confirm.

            - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
            been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
            have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

            - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
            is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
            onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
            Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


            ## Assumptions


            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
            Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
            without new state approval

            - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
            Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

            - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
            validated before close without a monitoring gap

            - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
            MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

            - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
            41 states (per the request).

            - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
            which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
            (structure not yet confirmed).

            '

          support_state: supplied
          source_type: workspace
          available_excerpt: "# Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor
            transition: continuity\n\n## Question\n\nResearch this issue for the dossier:
            Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
            the SaaS contract terminates at close. Harbor's monitoring contract ends
            at close. A failed or untested change could create an immediate gap in
            detection, records, and case handling.\nLawyer's accepted priorities (private
            matter context):\nMake KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring continuity
            formal close and migration gates.: These linked controls affect the full
            migrated population and can create immediate exposure that is difficult
            to repair later.\nProposed date leads; resolve each reference in saved
            records before using it: [{\"role\": \"target_close\", \"value\": \"2026-11-15\",
            \"source_reference_id\": \"FACT-20260909-182bcc\", \"note\": \"The recorded
            fact states that close is targeted for Nov 15. The year is inferred from
            the September 2026 record date and should be confirmed.\"}, {\"role\":
            \"planned_customer_migration\", \"value\": \"day 1 post-close\", \"source_reference_id\":
            \"FACT-20260909-551367\", \"note\": \"This is the actual saved plan. Do
            not replace it with the hypothetical November 15 migration date.\"}, {\"role\":
            \"planned_marketing_launch\", \"value\": \"close+1\", \"source_reference_id\":
            \"FACT-20260909-19aebc\", \"note\": \"The record does not define whether
            close+1 means one calendar day or one business day after close.\"}]\n\n##
            Working Analysis\n\n**No external authority retrieved**\n\nI have the
            framework-level support from the saved model act. Before composing, let
            me confirm real record IDs for the synthesis (assumption and issue identifiers)
            from the matter's saved records.\n\nNo oversized model request was sent.\n\n##
            Sources surfaced\n\n- Supplied source: [issues.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-27b344a827f0cf86ced5.md)
            [source:SRC-LOCAL-27b344a827f0cf86ced5]\n  Available excerpt:\n  > # Issues
            and workstreams\n  > \n  > - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic
            Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor's
            MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n  > - BSA/AML an\n- Supplied source:
            [facts.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md)
            [source:SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c]\n  Available excerpt:\n  > # Known
            Facts\n  > \n  > - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
            Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n  > - Migration moves 240k consumer users and
            12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-clos\n- Supplied
            source: [DOR-20260912-1bfef3.md](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-98171c064736338012ae.md)
            [source:SRC-LOCAL-98171c064736338012ae]\n  Available excerpt:\n  > ##
            Suggested dossier plan\n  > \n  > Review the suggested priorities below.\n
            \ > \n  > \n  > \n  > > Preparation analysis did not complete (TimeoutError).
            The suggested priorities fall back to the existing issue order.\n- Retrieved
            source: [PDF CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 27, characters
            0–1943](https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf)
            [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538|Page 27, characters 0–1943]\n  Available
            excerpt:\n  > 27 \n  >  \n  > (c) \n  > The audited financial statements
            shall include or be accompanied by a \n  > certificate of opinion of the
            independent certified public accountant or independent public \n  > accountant
            that is satisf\n- Retrieved source: [PDF CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
            Act — Page 28, characters 0–2132](https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf)
            [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538|Page 28, characters 0–2132]\n  Available

            with the [Commissioner] within one business \n  > day after the licensee

            \ > (1) \n  > the filing of a\n- Retrieved source: [PDF CSBS Money Transmission

            \ > (6) \n  > a list of the last known names and addresses of all of the
            \n  > licensee's authorized deleg\n- Retrieved source: [PDF CSBS Money
            Transmission Modernization Act — Page 12, characters 0–2795](https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf)
            [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538|Page 12, characters 0–2795]\n  Available

            bond filed by a licensee, provided that \n  > confidential information,
            including, but not limited to, prices and fees for such bond is \n  >
            redacted; \n  > (5) \n  > Copies of a\n\n## Last-mile work for counsel\n\n-
            Confirm the facts that could change the recommendation.\n- Verify any
