        inputs:
          business_question:
            question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
            text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
              review before the Nov 15 close?
            revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
          facts:
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
              weeks out).
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
            text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
            text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at
              Mosaic's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
            text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
            text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC'd.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
            text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor's assets)
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
            text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
              another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
            text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
              Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
              for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e

          - question_id: Q-SAR
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and
              could affect the deal itself.

              in diligence.

          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?

              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.

              for the four new markets.

            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-df5dd9f25cf0547e2d1e.md
            revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
            file_revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

            reported: false
            passages: &id115
            - start: 0
              end: 3962
              text: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '
            source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                the acquisition

                underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s
                independent CIP/AML obligations

                Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                money transmission or consumer protection implications

              text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant that
                is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the
                certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order
                the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
                to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent
                public accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized
                Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of
                authorized delegates within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20
                The [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS
                for the submission of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)]
                provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements
                of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
                include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany
                legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3)
                \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing
                address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny
                fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number,
                and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10)
                \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
                \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny
                other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect
                to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21
                \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to implement state use
                of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21
                Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section
                7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to
                prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"

              text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of
                the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing
                of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States
                Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified
                from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe
                filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
                the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding
                for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making of a general
                assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement
                of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country
                in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA
                licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three
                business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
                of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of
                the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in control of the
                licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized
                delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports.
                \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required
                by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity
                reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and
                other federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely
                filing of \na complete and accurate report required under this [Section
                7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant with
                the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a)
                \nLicensee shall maintain the following records, for determining its
                \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na
                record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2)
                \na general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability,
                capital, income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and
                bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money
                transmission obligations;\n"

                are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days'
                notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained
                by the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to
                inspection by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n
                \nARTICLE VIII \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship
                Between Licensee and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section
                8.01], \"remit\" means to make direct payments of money to \na licensee
                or its representative authorized to receive money or to deposit money
                in a bank in an \naccount specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore
                a licensee is authorized to conduct business through an authorized
                \ndelegate or allows a person to act as the licensee's authorized
                delegate, the licensee must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update as necessary,
                written policies and procedures \nreasonably designed to ensure that
                the licensee's authorized delegates comply with \napplicable state
                and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract that complies
                with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct a reasonable risk-based
                background investigation sufficient \nfor the licensee to determine
                whether the authorized delegate has complied and will likely \ncomply
                with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate
                must operate in full compliance with this [Act]. \n(d) \nThe written
                contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed by the \nlicensee
                and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"

              text: "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a licensee,

                to, prices and fees for such bond is \nredacted; \n(5) \nCopies of
                any non-confidential final orders of the [Department] \nrelating to
                any violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act];
                and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under
                this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner]
                may conduct an examination or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized
                delegate or otherwise take independent action authorized by this [Act]
                or by \na rule adopted or order issued under this [Act] as reasonably
                necessary or appropriate to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations
                implementing this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe
                Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may:
                \n(1) \nconduct an examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner]
                may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction
                with an examination \nconducted by representatives of other state
                agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal government;
                \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another state agency or
                an agency \nof another state or of the federal government, or a report
                prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which on being accepted
                is considered for all purposes as an official report \nof the [Commissioner];
                and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under oath a key individual or employee
                of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate and require the person to produce
                records regarding any \nmatter related to the condition and business
                of the licensee or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized
                delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and
                complete access to, all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably
                require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records must be provided
                at the location and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner],
                provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate record \nproduction
                standards and examination procedures when such standards will reasonably
                achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless
                otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee shall pay all
                \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination of the
                licensee or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner] is
                encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination requests
                in \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee to obtain records
                located outside of the U.S., including but not limited \nto evidence
                demonstrating when an outstanding money transmission obligation has
                been extinguished; and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as
                provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"

        available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


          - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
          out).

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and
          full access to Mosaic''s product set.

          - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

          - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay
          holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
          pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
          onboarded before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
          launching close+1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

          - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
          already KYC''d.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results
          exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
          before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

          - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
          buys Harbor''s assets)

          - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
          institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
          required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

          - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last
          year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
          Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
          own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

          - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
          the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
          AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
          confirm.

          - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been
          reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have
          not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s
          licenses for the four new markets.


          ## Assumptions


          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
          Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
          without new state approval

          - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
          Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

          - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
          before close without a monitoring gap

          - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
          MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41
          states (per the request).

          - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
          which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
          (structure not yet confirmed).

          '

          combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition

          - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
          underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
          CIP/AML obligations

          - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
          ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

          - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
          the SaaS contract terminates at close

          - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money
          transmission or consumer protection implications

          - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
          -->

          '
        selected_passages: *id116
        content_truncated: false
        source_label: SRC-LOCAL-27b344a827f0cf86ced5.md

        support_state: supplied
        source_type: workspace
        available_excerpt: "# Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor
          transition: continuity\n\n## Question\n\nResearch this issue for the dossier:
          Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
          the SaaS contract terminates at close. Harbor's monitoring contract ends
          at close. A failed or untested change could create an immediate gap in detection,
          records, and case handling.\nLawyer's accepted priorities (private matter
          context):\nMake KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring continuity formal
          close and migration gates.: These linked controls affect the full migrated
          population and can create immediate exposure that is difficult to repair
          later.\nProposed date leads; resolve each reference in saved records before
          using it: [{\"role\": \"target_close\", \"value\": \"2026-11-15\", \"source_reference_id\":
          \"FACT-20260909-182bcc\", \"note\": \"The recorded fact states that close
          is targeted for Nov 15. The year is inferred from the September 2026 record
          date and should be confirmed.\"}, {\"role\": \"planned_customer_migration\",
          \"value\": \"day 1 post-close\", \"source_reference_id\": \"FACT-20260909-551367\",
          \"note\": \"This is the actual saved plan. Do not replace it with the hypothetical
          November 15 migration date.\"}, {\"role\": \"planned_marketing_launch\",
          \"value\": \"close+1\", \"source_reference_id\": \"FACT-20260909-19aebc\",
          \"note\": \"The record does not define whether close+1 means one calendar
          day or one business day after close.\"}]\n\n## Working Analysis\n\n**No
          external authority retrieved**\n\nI have the framework-level support from
          the saved model act. Before composing, let me confirm real record IDs for

          records.\n\nNo oversized model request was sent.\n\n## Sources surfaced\n\n-

          Facts\n  > \n  > - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted

          business accounts into Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-clos\n- Supplied

      - source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
        source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
        title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
        extraction_state: complete
        selected_passages:
        - *id118
        support_state: retrieved
        url: https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf
        original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin
        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md
        source_hash: 512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705
        source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 27,
          characters 0–1943'
        unit_id: p000027
        locator: Page 27, characters 0–1943
        available_excerpt: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
          or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified
          public accountant or independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory
          in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion
          is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order the licensee to take any action
          as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable the independent or
          certified public accountant or \nindependent public accountant to remove
          the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach
          licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45 days \nof
          the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized and
          encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report required by
          this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent
          with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate
          report shall include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1)
          \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3)
          \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing
          address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious
          or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and email \n(9)
          \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting
          as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders
          pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information the [Commissioner]
          reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized delegate. \nSection
          7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed
          to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR)
          process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy
          Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality
          to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"
      - source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
        source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
        title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
        extraction_state: complete
        selected_passages:
        - *id119
        support_state: retrieved
        url: https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf
        original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin
        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md
        source_hash: 80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973
        source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 28,
          characters 0–2132'
        unit_id: p000028
        locator: Page 28, characters 0–2132
        available_excerpt: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the
          [Commissioner] within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to
          know of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing
          of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy
          Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified from \ntime to
          time, for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition
          by or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any other
          judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or reorganization,
          or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors;
          or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense
          in a state or country in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed.
          \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three
          business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of
          any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee
          or of a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony;
          or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
          \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
          delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
          record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set forth
          in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining to
          money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate report
          required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency
          is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection
          7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records, for
          determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years:
          \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold;
          \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability,
          capital, income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank
          reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission
          obligations;\n"
      - source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
        source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
        title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
        extraction_state: complete
        selected_passages:
        - *id120
        support_state: retrieved
        url: https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf
        original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin
        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000029.md
        source_hash: 5b35638f1a8d6575d9fb47895535602e82ed0f84fca696af8c017016862d94c9
        source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 29,
          characters 0–1920'
        unit_id: p000029
        locator: Page 29, characters 0–1920
        available_excerpt: "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission
          obligation \npaid within the [three]-year period; \n(6) \na list of the
          last known names and addresses of all of the \nlicensee's authorized delegates;
          and \n(7) \nany other records the [Commissioner] reasonably requires \nby
          rule. \n(b) \nThe items specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained
          in any form of \nrecord. \n(c) \nRecords specified in [Section 7.06(a)]
          may be maintained outside this state \nif they are made accessible to the
          [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days' notice that is sent in \na record.
          \n(d) \nAll records maintained by the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)]
          \nare open to inspection by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)].
          \n \nARTICLE VIII \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between
          Licensee and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\"
          means to make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its representative
          authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an \naccount
          specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized to conduct
          business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows a person to act as the
          licensee's authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update
          as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably designed to ensure
          that the licensee's authorized delegates comply with \napplicable state
          and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract that complies with
          [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct a reasonable risk-based background
          investigation sufficient \nfor the licensee to determine whether the authorized
          delegate has complied and will likely \ncomply with applicable state and
          federal law. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate must operate in full compliance

          \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under this [Act]. \nSection
          4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct an examination
          or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate or otherwise take
          independent action authorized by this [Act] or by \na rule adopted or order
          issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary or appropriate to administer
          \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing this [Act], and other
          applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT.
          \ The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct an examination either on-site
          or off-site as the \n[Commissioner] may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct
          an examination in conjunction with an examination \nconducted by representatives
          of other state agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal
          government; \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another state agency
          or an agency \nof another state or of the federal government, or a report
          prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which on being accepted is
          considered for all purposes as an official report \nof the [Commissioner];
          and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under oath a key individual or employee of
          a \nlicensee or authorized delegate and require the person to produce records
          regarding any \nmatter related to the condition and business of the licensee
          or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate shall
          provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and complete access to,
          all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably require to \nconduct a complete
          examination. The records must be provided at the location and in the format
          \nspecified by the [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize
          multistate record \nproduction standards and examination procedures when
          such standards will reasonably achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section
          4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee
          shall pay all \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination

          when an outstanding money transmission obligation has been extinguished;
          and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as provided to the licensee
          by the bank.\n"

            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b.md
            revision: 916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac

            passages: &id122
            - start: 0
              end: 1441
              text: '# Issues and workstreams


                - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
                the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
                the acquisition

                - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
                underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s
                independent CIP/AML obligations

                - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                money transmission or consumer protection implications

                - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                -->

                - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
                <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

                - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!--
                issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->

                - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
                -->

                - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
                -->

                - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
                -->

                - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
                issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->

                '
            source_version: 916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac

            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
            revision: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

            passages: &id123
            - start: 0
              end: 3962
              text: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '
            source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

            - start: 0

              text: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter dossier)


                Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated
                Sep 9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record; direction
                unchanged.


                ## Current position


                Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review
                before the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before the
                deal terms are settled, not merely before launch. This is not "just
                a data migration": the day-1 plan depends on results the records show
                are unconfirmed — license coverage in the added markets, the ability
                to rely on Harbor''s KYC without the underlying records, and a monitoring
                cutover with no gap.


                Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


                - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.**
                The plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for an
                asset purchase. If approvals are missing, those markets are a post-close
                target, not day-1 access. (The number of added states is itself unresolved
                — see Record conflicts.)


                - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
                on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing
                documents can keep full access without re-verification or limits.


                - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether
                monitoring transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most
                decision-changing item because it can affect deal protections and
                how affected customers are handled at migration.


                The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms side
                of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but each must
                be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs documents
                not in the readable record.


                What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
                data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review
                protocol for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching
                the added markets on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding of
                users whose verification cannot be evidenced; the monitoring cutover
                unless a tested no-gap design or a bridge exists; the bonus until
                its terms are reviewed.


                This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and
                preparing a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s recommendation,
                not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged: day-1 full
                migration, no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses, bonus
                at close+1. The only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep 9 intake
                answers (asset purchase; compliance to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs
                unreviewed; use/assume Harbor''s licenses). A complete dossier rewrite
                was submitted as a tracked revision on Sep 10 and, per the record,
                left the current dossier unchanged pending acceptance; generating
                this draft records no new decision.


                ## Decision question


                Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
                before the Nov 15 close?


                ## Issues


                The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep
                9 initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s
                "four issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML,
                alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its
                ISS identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material, so
                no issue IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified
                in this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.


                Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
                records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources
                ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial
                "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d])
                later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
                and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
                ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here. Every
                legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead, not verified
                support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**. Each issue gets
                an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers in the nine
                captured documents were not readable in this run and should be merged
                when available.


                ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


                **Current answer**


                Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
                carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
                legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until
                a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control
                approval in the transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed
                entity performs the transmission — the added markets should be treated
                as post-close, not part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic holds
                its own license, the account migration may trigger state notices or
                filings (unverified).


                **Rule and support**


                State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status
                as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
                licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
                required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business
                [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the
                CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal
                MSB registration (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380) is a separate requirement
                and does not substitute for state licensure [**Needs checking**].
                The precise research question: for each state where Mosaic lacks a
                license and Harbor holds one, what route lets Mosaic lawfully serve
                migrated customers — new license, license transfer, change-of-control
                approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement — on what timeline, and
                what customer or regulator notices accompany the change?


                **Application**


                Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
                Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
                licenses"; full acce'

              text: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov 15)


                **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
                migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest turn
                ("Generate the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds comparisons
                are supporting work; they do not change that question. The record
                contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered issues
                are `open`, and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is structured
                — was left open with no answer.


                **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data migration."
                The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated event: on day
                1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its own licensed product
                set with no re-verification, repoints monitoring, and launches a cash
                offer — under an asset-purchase structure in which nothing about Harbor''s
                licenses or compliance record transfers by default. The operative
                question is therefore not "can we inherit Harbor''s status," but **"what
                must Mosaic obtain, file, decide or preserve in its own name before
                Nov 15, and which parts of the stated deal upside are not actually
                available at close."**


                **Three premises the record lets us test**


                1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment
                CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to 252k
                accounts.

                2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on
                the arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state
                union yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are never
                named; and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests on an
                assumption the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]),
                against the saved position that transferability should not be relied
                on without a state rule, approval or written regulator position.

                3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved.
                Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown,
                and the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in
                2024; only pass/fail survives).


                **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9 weeks
                as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and preserve
                the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and schedule
                remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate the monitoring
                cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent, new customer terms
                and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate only in the overlapping
                states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts with limits — a
                scoped migration rather than the full one.


                **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing
                (44-state footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users;
                SAR and alert handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor
                transition at close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and
                material: **migration data handling and customer notice** (the piece
                the request actually calls "just a data migration," never analyzed);
                **pre-close papering** (closing conditions, interim operation, allocation
                of the alert/SAR and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere);
                and **post-close access to Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records
                live in the SaaS system whose contract ends at close).


                **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business question,
                time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


                1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else
                is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the deal itself;
                it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a filing is late
                or an account must be excluded; and the records needed to answer it
                may become inaccessible at close.

                2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify,
                or restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification" is
                available at all for the largest population; the underlying documents
                cannot be recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week
                program that has to be decided before close, not after.

                3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull
                them from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being sold
                on, state timelines are the longest external dependency and cannot
                be compressed, and serving a state without authority is a violation
                later paperwork cannot undo.


                **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
                KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
                position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
                — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
                licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog
                read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.


                **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
                and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and
                some prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions
                are not findings about this acquisition. The licensing research has
                **no citable support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one
                output headed "No external authority retrieved"), and repeated "research
                queued/running" messages are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b]
                still calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase
                is recorded and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date`
                field (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12
                — treat it as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where
                the close date itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured
                afterwards; it is not the same as the top-three ranking.


                *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
                facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing packet
                was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated as fallible
                synthesis.*

                '
            source_version: 8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73

        available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


          - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
          out).

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and
          full access to Mosaic''s product set.

          - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

          - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay
          holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
          pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
          onboarded before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
          launching close+1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

          - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.

          - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were
          already KYC''d.

          - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results
          exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
          before 2023.

          - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
          engine on day 1.

          - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

          - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
          buys Harbor''s assets)

          - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
          institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
          required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

          - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last
          year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
          Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its
          own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

          - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
          the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s
          AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must
          confirm.

          - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been
          reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have
          not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

          - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s
          licenses for the four new markets.


          ## Assumptions


          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
          Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
          without new state approval

          - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
          Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

          - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
          before close without a monitoring gap

          - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
          MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

          - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41
          states (per the request).

          - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
          which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
          (structure not yet confirmed).

          '

        available_excerpt: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter

          ## Current position


          Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review before
          the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before the deal terms
          are settled, not merely before launch. This is not "just a data migration":
          the day-1 plan depends on results the records show are unconfirmed — license
          coverage in the added markets, the ability to rely on Harbor''s KYC without
          the underlying records, and a monitoring cutover with no gap.


          Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


          - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.** The
          plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for an asset purchase.
          If approvals are missing, those markets are a post-close target, not day-1
          access. (The number of added states is itself unresolved — see Record conflicts.)


          - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
          on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing documents
          can keep full access without re-verification or limits.


          - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether monitoring
          transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most decision-changing
          item because it can affect deal protections and how affected customers are
          handled at migration.


          The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms side of
          the data move do not block close on today''s record, but each must be reviewed
          before its own go-live point and each needs documents not in the readable
          record.


          What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance data
          pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review protocol for

          on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding of users whose verification
